FLAGS:
• FCCR reinstatement-readiness analysis (Stabilization Milestone M4) is due from the borrower to the lender on September 30, 2026, about two weeks from this review, and should clarify what happens when the legacy FCCR covenant's suspension window ends.
  • The EBITDA reconciling item embedded in the borrower's own certified "Covenant EBITDA" ($553,353.26 per month, $6.64M annualized) is not supported by any agreement text located to date and remains excluded from this analysis's EBITDA definition.
  • An Interim goodwill reassessment required as of March 31, 2026 had not been completed as of the June 2026 reporting package.
  • Restructuring accounting (TDR framework, instrument-level 10% modification test, CODI, and Section 382) remains PROVISIONAL through the June 2026 package; successor balance-sheet figures could still restate.
FORWARD_STRESS: If the FCCR mechanically reinstates at 1.2000x on January 1, 2027 while the informational ratio continues along its June 2026 trend (0.3682x, worsening every quarter since suspension), the facility would show a breach absent a further amendment or a different outcome from the pending reinstatement-readiness analysis due September 30, 2026.
IS_OBSERVATIONS:
• Revenue rose 2.2% month over month to $13.16M in June but sits 17.4% (about $2.8M) below the Approved Stabilization Budget's $15.9M plan for the month, and 17.0% below budget quarter to date ($38.7M vs $46.6M).
  • Gross margin improved to 33.5% in June from 31.6% in May, continuing the trend since the March 2026 restructuring boundary.
  • EBITDA rose 23.3% month over month to $1.55M (11.8% margin), beating the $1.3M June budget by 19.9%, though the quarter-to-date beat is a thinner 7.1% against a $3.6M budget.
  • Net income turned positive in June ($84.8K) after a $205.4K loss in May.
  • Gross Profit and Gross Margin figures shown against budget are not meaningful for this borrower: the Approved Stabilization Budget only plans Revenue and EBITDA, so those other lines compare against a proxy row rather than a real plan.
LIQUIDITY_READ:
• Cash of $18.82M at June 2026 sits $8.82M (88%) above the $10.0M Minimum Liquidity covenant floor and matches the borrower's own certified figure exactly.
  • Cash has risen every month since the March 2026 recapitalization ($18.14M, $18.14M, $18.41M, $18.82M), funded by positive operating cash flow rather than new borrowing.
  • Cash is running 11.9% (about $2.0M) above the $16.81M plan for June.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: The most time-sensitive open question is what happens to the FCCR covenant when its stated December 31, 2026 suspension window ends: the credit agreement's own text supports a literal reading of mechanical reinstatement at 1.2000x on January 1, 2027, but Stabilization Milestone M4 (an FCCR reinstatement-readiness analysis, due from the borrower September 30, 2026) suggests the lender may act on the informational trend before that date instead. Separately, the EBITDA reconciling item the borrower's certificates use ($553,353.26 per month, added to this model's Reported EBITDA to reach "Covenant EBITDA") is not supported by any agreement text located to date; resolving it, ideally against a longer-form version of the credit agreement if one exists, would settle both the FCCR's true informational level and the Fixed Charges definition's roughly $9.1M TTM gap to the certified figure. The restructuring's TDR framework, instrument-level modification test, CODI, and Section 382 conclusions also remain open with the borrower's accountants.
REVENUE_QUALITY_NOTES: Revenue is fee-for-service, billed to a diversified payer mix (Medicare, Commercial, Medicaid, Workers' Compensation, and Self-Pay) across five regional operating subsidiaries and fifteen clinical sites, with no single payer class exceeding about 27% of the June 2026 receivables balance. It is transactional rather than contractually recurring: no ARR or retention metric is reported, and volumes depend on patient visits and procedures at each site rather than a committed book of business. The revenue shortfall against the Approved Stabilization Budget (-17.4% in June, -17.0% quarter to date) reads as a volume and site-productivity gap on the information available, separate from pricing or payer mix.
SUMMARY_COLLATERAL: Pledged collateral totals $166.4M at June 2026: cash $18.8M, accounts receivable $20.9M, PP&E net $48.6M, and goodwill $78.1M. That covers the $49.7M of secured debt 3.3x on an all-assets basis or 1.8x excluding goodwill, but only 0.8x on liquid collateral (cash plus receivables) alone, so the cushion depends on the illiquid asset base. Goodwill is flat month over month at $78.1M and down 2.4% year over year; total pledged components are essentially flat month over month.
SUMMARY_COVENANTS: Minimum Liquidity is the only actively tested financial covenant this period and passes with room: $18.8M against the $10.0M floor, matching the borrower's own certificate exactly. The legacy 1.2000x FCCR test remains suspended (informational only) through December 31, 2026; the certified informational ratio was 0.3682x at June 2026, below 1.2000x and worsening every quarter since the Q3 2025 suspension (1.43x, 1.05x, 0.67x, 0.37x). The nearest live risk is this spec's modeled FCCR reinstatement at 1.2000x effective January 1, 2027 -- clearing that level from today's informational trend would need a substantial EBITDA recovery or Fixed Charges reduction beyond what June's run-rate shows.
SUMMARY_LIQUIDITY: Cash ended June at $18.8M, $8.8M (88%) above the $10.0M covenant floor, and has risen every month since the March 2026 recapitalization ($18.1M, $18.1M, $18.4M, $18.8M). The increase is funded by operating cash flow ($692K in June) rather than new borrowing -- financing cash flow was a modest net use of $51K, the facility's scheduled amortization payment. No month has shown a cash decline since the recapitalization.
SUMMARY_OUTLOOK: The governing question for this credit is whether the post-restructuring operating recovery -- revenue and EBITDA both improving month over month, with the borrower's own site-operations reporting showing a declining weak-site count and lower agency-labor reliance -- closes enough of the gap to the stabilization budget before the FCCR's informational path forces a decision. The borrower owes the lender its FCCR reinstatement-readiness analysis (Stabilization Milestone M4) by September 30, 2026, about two weeks from this review, which should clarify whether reinstatement, a further amendment, or continued suspension follows. Restructuring accounting (the TDR framework, instrument-level modification test, CODI, and Section 382 conclusions) also remains open and could still move successor balance-sheet figures once resolved.
SUMMARY_UPDATE: June revenue was $13.2M, 17.4% (about $2.8M) below the $15.9M Approved Stabilization Budget for the month, though up 2.2% from May's $12.9M. Quarter to date (Apr-Jun, since the March 2026 restructuring), revenue of $38.7M runs 17.0% (about $7.9M) below the $46.6M budget over the same span. EBITDA beat budget in June at $1.5M against a $1.3M plan (+$257K, +19.9%), though the quarter-to-date beat is thinner at +7.1% (+$259K) against a $3.6M plan -- lighter opex run-rate is offsetting the top-line shortfall rather than volume recovering to plan.

summary_blocks.SUMMARY_COVENANTS: one sentence when everything passes with room; otherwise the failing or governing leg, the certified-vs-model gap, and the nearest tight test with what clearing it takes
summary_blocks.SUMMARY_LIQUIDITY: period-end cash against the floor, where the cash came from (earned, borrowed, working capital), months of runway when burning, and the expected direction with its basis

summary_blocks.bad_news: a miss, a breach or a stretch is written in its home block with the same syntax as a beat — there is no separate red-flags list, and a fired concern must not be left out of its block
summary_blocks.cadence: the renderer titles the first block from the period: a March/June/September/December period reads 'Quarterly update' and its prose covers the quarter and the year so far; any other month reads 'Monthly update' and covers the month and the year so far
summary_blocks.numbers: round to $X.XM / $XXXK in these five blocks; full precision lives in the tables, where every figure is click-traceable
summary_blocks.what: the executive summary is the analyst's one-pager for the deal team: five labelled prose blocks, each 2-5 sentences, written the way a portfolio review reads — the figure, its comparator (vs Budget, vs prior year), then the driver. The template owns the labels; write only the prose.
